SOURCE: docs/lgx-reference.md — LGX reference
================================================================

# LGX reference

Generated from the compiler's catalogues by `lgx_reference_lock`; every example below was parsed by the compiler to produce its row. Do not edit this file: run `./scripts/release/lgx/gen-reference.sh`. [Frontend](frontend.md) teaches the same constructs in order, with pages you can run.

## Template tags

What a `View:` holds, one row per construct.

| Template | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<p class="note">Saved</p>` | An HTML element. It closes with its end tag; a void element (`input`, `br`, `img` …) takes none. |
| `Saved` | Text. A run that is only whitespace and holds a newline is formatting and is dropped; other runs collapse to one space. |
| `{count}` | The value, escaped. |
| `{title \| truncate 20}` | The value through a filter: this hole is `truncate(title, 20)`. Filters apply left to right. |
| `{raw trustedHtml}` | The value inserted as markup, unescaped — only for text already made safe. |
| `{if count is 0:}<p>none</p>{else if count is 1:}<p>one</p>{else:}<p>many</p>{end}` | The first arm whose condition holds; `{else:}` when none does. |
| `{for each todo in todos, keyed by todo's id, at index i:}<li>{i}. {todo's title}</li>{else:}<li>nothing yet</li>{end}` | One body per item; the `{else:}` arm renders when the collection is empty. See Loop bindings. |
| `{inspect found:}{when Some (name):}<p>{name}</p>{when None:}<p>not found</p>{end}` | The arm whose pattern matches the value. |
| `{let left be length of todos}` | A name bound for the rest of the enclosing scope. |
| `{extends Site}` | This view fills the named layout's blocks. It is the first thing in the view, or absent. |
| `{block main:}<p>nothing here yet</p>{end}` | A layout slot, with the content shown when the page fills nothing. |
| `{block main}` | A layout slot a page fills. |
| `{children}` | Where the caller's markup lands inside a component. |
| `<Badge label={title}/>` | A placed component. A capitalised tag is a component; its attributes are its declared props. |
| `{# a note for the reader #}` | A comment; dropped. |

Spellings from other template languages are refused with the LGX spelling, rather than read as a hole naming a variable:

| Written | LGX spelling |
|---|---|
| `elif` | `else if` |
| `elsif` | `else if` |
| `elseif` | `else if` |
| `otherwise` | `else` |
| `endif` | `end` |
| `endfor` | `end` |

## Directives on elements

| Element | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<button on-click={add}>Add</button>` | On `click`, runs the action `add`. |
| `<button on-click={remove(todo's id)}>Remove</button>` | On `click`, calls `remove(todo's id)`. |
| `<form on-submit.prevent={add}></form>` | On `submit`, runs the action `add`, qualified by `.prevent` (see Event modifiers). |
| `<input on-keydown.enter={add}>` | On `keydown`, runs the action `add`, qualified by `.enter` (see Event modifiers). |
| `<input bind={draft}>` | Two-way binding between the control and the state field `draft`. |
| `<li class:done={todo's done}>{todo's title}</li>` | The class `done` is present while the condition holds. |
| `<a href="/todos/{todo's id}">open</a>` | A computed `href`, escaped. |
| `<img src={avatarUrl} alt="">` | A computed `src`, escaped. |
| `<input type="text">` | A literal `type`. |
| `<input disabled>` | A boolean attribute: `disabled` is on while it is present. |

## Event modifiers

An `on-<event>` directive takes qualifiers after dots. Every tier reads them through one catalogue; a word it does not know is a compile error.

Behaviour — how the event is treated, on any event:

| Qualifier | Meaning | Browser build |
|---|---|---|
| `.prevent` | The browser's default action (a form posting, a link following) does not run. | yes |
| `.stop` | The event does not propagate to the element's ancestors. | yes |
| `.once` | The listener answers the first event and is then removed. | yes |
| `.capture` | The listener runs in the capture phase, before the target's own listeners. | yes |
| `.passive` | The listener promises not to cancel the default action. | yes |

Keys — one per handler, on `on-keydown`, `on-keyup`, `on-keypress` only. The handler answers when the browser's `KeyboardEvent.key` is the value shown, compared without case.

| Qualifier | `KeyboardEvent.key` | Browser build |
|---|---|---|
| `.enter` | `"Enter"` | yes |
| `.escape` | `"Escape"` | yes |
| `.space` | `" "` | yes |
| `.tab` | `"Tab"` | yes |
| `.backspace` | `"Backspace"` | yes |
| `.delete` | `"Delete"` | yes |
| `.arrowup` | `"ArrowUp"` | yes |
| `.arrowdown` | `"ArrowDown"` | yes |
| `.arrowleft` | `"ArrowLeft"` | yes |
| `.arrowright` | `"ArrowRight"` | yes |
| `.home` | `"Home"` | yes |
| `.end` | `"End"` | yes |
| `.pageup` | `"PageUp"` | yes |
| `.pagedown` | `"PageDown"` | yes |
| any single printable character, such as `.a` | that character | yes |

System keys — named by the catalogue and refused on every tier:

| Qualifier | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `.ctrl` | A system-key qualifier (`.ctrl`) is refused: no tier delivers modifier-key state to a handler. |
| `.alt` | A system-key qualifier (`.alt`) is refused: no tier delivers modifier-key state to a handler. |
| `.shift` | A system-key qualifier (`.shift`) is refused: no tier delivers modifier-key state to a handler. |
| `.meta` | A system-key qualifier (`.meta`) is refused: no tier delivers modifier-key state to a handler. |

The refusals:

- A word the catalogue does not know is refused, naming the nearest one: `.stpo` → `.stop`.
- A key qualifier on an event that carries no key is refused: `.enter` on `click`. Keys belong on `on-keydown`, `on-keyup`, `on-keypress`.
- One handler answers one key: `.enter` with `.escape` is refused; write a handler per key.
- A system-key qualifier (`.ctrl`) is refused: no tier delivers modifier-key state to a handler.
- `.prevent` and `.passive` on one handler are refused: a passive listener ignores `.prevent`, so a browser would run the default action anyway. Write one or the other.

## Triggers

A sentence in a component's `Actions:` that runs its indented body when something happens. The form is how a compiler message quotes the sentence.

| Sentence | Form | Runs |
|---|---|---|
| `When the page loads:` | `When the page loads:` | Once, when the page mounts, before its first paint. |
| `When this component appears:` | `When this component appears:` | When this component enters the page. |
| `When this component disappears:` | `When this component disappears:` | When this component leaves the page. |
| `When "#save" is clicked:` | `When "…" is …:` | On `click` at that element. |
| `When the user types in "#draft":` | `When "…" is …:` | On `input` at that element. |
| `When the user presses Enter in "#draft":` | `When "…" is …:` | On `keydown` at that element, for the `Enter` key. |
| `When the user presses Escape:` | `When the user presses …:` | On the `Escape` key, anywhere on the page. |
| `When n changes:` | `When … changes:` | After a turn changes this component's `n`. |
| `When Session's name changes:` | `When <Store>'s … changes:` | After a turn changes the store's field `Session's name`, in every component that uses the store. |
| `Every 60 seconds:` | `Every … seconds:` | Repeatedly, once per period. |
| `Every 60 seconds as tick:` | `Every … seconds:` | Repeatedly, once per period; named, so `Stop the timer tick.` cancels it. |
| `After 5 seconds:` | `After … seconds:` | Once, after the delay. |
| `After 5 seconds as reminder:` | `After … seconds:` | Once, after the delay; named, so `Stop the timer reminder.` cancels it before it fires. |
| `When a message arrives on "news" (body: Text):` | `When a message arrives on …:` | On each message published on the topic; `body` binds its payload as `Text`. |
| `When an action fails (why: Text):` | `When an action fails …:` | After a turn fails and is rolled back; `why` binds the failure message. |
| `When a fetch fails (url: Text) and (why: Text):` | `When a fetch fails …:` | After any request fails; `url` binds its URL and `why` the reason. |
| `When the route changes:` | `When the route changes:` | After every navigation. |
| `When the app goes offline:` | `When the app goes offline:` | When the network goes. |
| `When the app comes back online:` | `When the app comes back online:` | When the network comes back. |
| `When the window resizes:` | `When the window resizes:` | When the window is resized. |
| `When the user scrolls to the bottom:` | `When the user scrolls to the bottom …:` | When the page is scrolled to its bottom. |
| `When the user scrolls to the bottom of "#list":` | `When the user scrolls to the bottom …:` | When that element is scrolled to its bottom. |
| `When a file is dropped on "#zone" (file: File):` | `When a file is dropped on …:` | When a file is dropped on that element; `file: File` binds the whole `File` record. |
| `When a file is dropped on "#zone" (name: Text):` | `When a file is dropped on …:` | When a file is dropped on that element; `name: Text` binds the file's name. |

`When "#sel" is <word>:` takes these words:

| Word | DOM event |
|---|---|
| `clicked` | `click` |
| `submitted` | `submit` |
| `focused` | `focus` |
| `blurred` | `blur` |
| `hovered` | `mouseover` |
| `changed` | `change` |
| `typed` | `input` |
| `keyed` | `keyup` |

## UI verbs

A verb is written in a component's `Actions:`, in a `## Test` that drives a page, or in both — the Where column.

| Sentence | Where | Does |
|---|---|---|
| `Focus "#draft".` | `Actions:` and `## Test` | Puts focus on the element and raises `focus`. |
| `Blur "#draft".` | `Actions:` and `## Test` | Takes focus off the element and raises `blur`. |
| `Hover "#draft".` | `Actions:` and `## Test` | Raises `mouseover` on the element. |
| `Navigate to "/todos".` | `Actions:` and `## Test` | Adds a history entry and routes to it. |
| `Reload the page.` | `Actions:` and `## Test` | Tears down every instance, listener and mounted root; browser storage stays. |
| `Scroll to "#draft".` | `Actions:` | Scrolls the element into view. |
| `Add class "shake" to "#draft".` | `Actions:` | Adds one class word to the element. |
| `Remove class "shake" from "#draft".` | `Actions:` | Removes one class word from the element. |
| `Select the text in "#draft".` | `Actions:` | Selects the text in the element. |
| `Copy draft to the clipboard.` | `Actions:` | Writes the text to the clipboard. |
| `Download draft as "notes.txt".` | `Actions:` | Hands the visitor the bytes as a file with that name. |
| `Replace the URL with "/todos?page=2".` | `Actions:` | Replaces the current history entry; no new entry. |
| `Go back.` | `Actions:` | Goes one history entry back. |
| `Set the title to "Todos".` | `Actions:` | Sets the document title. |
| `Save draft as "draft".` | `Actions:` | Writes the value to browser storage under the key. |
| `Load "draft" into draft.` | `Actions:` | Reads the key from browser storage into a state field. |
| `Forget "draft".` | `Actions:` | Removes the key from browser storage. |
| `Notify "Saved.".` | `Actions:` | Shows a notification. |
| `Notify "Saved." as success.` | `Actions:` | Shows a notification in a tone: `success` or `error`. |
| `Publish draft on "chat".` | `Actions:` | Sends the message on a relay topic; this page's own subscribers hear it once. |
| `Toggle done.` | `Actions:` | Flips a `Bool` state field. |
| `Call Session's login with "ada".` | `Actions:` | Runs a store's action, with arguments after `with`. |
| `Stop the timer refresh.` | `Actions:` | Cancels a named timer. |
| `Start the timer refresh.` | `Actions:` | Arms a named timer again from now, reading its period afresh. |
| `Click "#save".` | `## Test` | Clicks the element. |
| `Submit "#form".` | `## Test` | Submits the form, as its submit button would. |
| `Choose "red" in "#colour".` | `## Test` | Picks the option with that value in a `<select>`. |
| `Type "milk" into "#draft".` | `## Test` | Types into the input, as a visitor would. |
| `Press "Enter" in "#draft".` | `## Test` | Presses the key at the element. |
| `Press "Escape".` | `## Test` | Presses the key at the element. |
| `Raise "offline".` | `## Test` | Causes an event that happens to the page, not to an element (`offline`, `online`, `resize`). |
| `Mount Badge.` | `## Test` | Creates the component's root instance and renders it. |

## Page queries

What a `## Test` asks the page, inside `Expect that …`.

| Query | Noun | Asks |
|---|---|---|
| `the text of "#n"` | `text` | The element's text content, its descendants' included. |
| `the count of ".row"` | `count` | How many elements match. |
| `the value of "#draft"` | `value` | An input's current value. |
| `"#n" is visible` | `visible` | Whether anything matches. |
| `"#n" is hidden` | `hidden` | Whether nothing matches — the complement of `visible`. |
| `"#save" is disabled` | `disabled` | Whether the match carries `disabled`. |
| `"#done" is checked` | `checked` | A checkbox's or radio's live checked state. |
| `"#draft" is focused` | `focused` | Whether focus is on the match. |
| `the journal` | `journal` | The actions that ran, in order, as a `Seq of Text`. |
| `the journal shows increment then decrement` | `journal ordering` | Whether the first action ran and the second ran after it, not necessarily next. |
| `the title` | `title` | The document title. |
| `the URL` | `URL` | The current path. |

## Loop bindings

`{for each todo in todos, keyed by todo's id, at index i:}<li>{i}. {todo's title}</li>{else:}<li>nothing yet</li>{end}`

| Binding | Value |
|---|---|
| `todo` | Each item of the collection in turn. |
| `todo's id` | The row's identity: a row whose key survives a re-render keeps its element and its state. |
| `i` | The item's position. The first item is 1, the position `item i of todos` reads. |
| `{else:}` | Renders instead when the collection is empty. |

## Filters

A filter is any function whose first parameter takes the hole's value: `{x | f a b}` is `f(x, a, b)`. The list-view filters come from `ui.lg`:

| Filter | Function | Answers |
|---|---|---|
| `{total \| pageCount perPage}` | `pageCount(total: Int, perPage: Int) -> Int` | How many pages `total` items make at `perPage` each. |
| `{page \| clampPage total perPage}` | `clampPage(page: Int, total: Int, perPage: Int) -> Int` | `page` brought inside `1` to `pageCount(total, perPage)`. |
| `{page \| pageStart perPage}` | `pageStart(page: Int, perPage: Int) -> Int` | The 1-based index of the first item on `page`. |
| `{page \| pageEnd perPage total}` | `pageEnd(page: Int, perPage: Int, total: Int) -> Int` | The 1-based index of the last item on `page`, never past `total`. |
| `{t \| truncate n}` | `truncate(t: Text, n: Int) -> Text` | `t` cut to at most `n` characters, marked with `…` when anything was removed. |
| `{n \| plural one many}` | `plural(n: Int, one: Text, many: Text) -> Text` | `n` with the word that agrees with it: `1 item`, `2 items`, `0 items`. |
| `{name \| initials}` | `initials(name: Text) -> Text` | The first letter of each word of `name`, run together: `Ada Lovelace` is `AL`. |

# The web standard library — forms, ui, session

Three modules of the standard library exist for web programs: `forms.lg` checks what a visitor
typed and says what was wrong, `ui.lg` does the page arithmetic and the wording a list view needs,
and `session.lg` signs the cookie a signed-in visitor carries. A program does not import them:
calling one of their functions is enough, and a `## Session` block calls `session.lg` for you.

Each section below builds a page on the pattern of the example project that uses the module, and
ends with the module's definitions — that table is generated from the module's own `## Note`s, so
it says what hover says.

## Forms — `forms.lg`

[`examples/signup_form`](../examples/signup_form) is the whole pattern. Every complaint about a
submission is a `FieldError` — the `field` it concerns and the `message` to show — and a
validation is a `Seq of FieldError` threaded through the checks, starting from `noErrors()`.

Three rules make the pattern safe to write:

- **The list is a sequence, not a map.** `errorFor(errors, "email")` answers `""` for a field with
  no complaint, so a template can write it under every input without asking first. A map would
  trap on the field that validated cleanly.
- **The first check to fail is the one shown.** `addError` leaves a field that already has a
  complaint alone, so order the checks from most fundamental to most particular: `checkRequired`
  before `checkMinLength`, or an empty box is told it is too short.
- **Validate on submit, not on every keystroke.** The complaints live in a plain `State:` field set
  by the submit action, so nothing scolds the visitor before they have tried once.

```logos-dom
## To validate (email: Text) and (password: Text) -> Seq of FieldError:
    Let mutable e be noErrors().
    Set e to checkRequired(e, "email", email).
    Set e to checkEmail(e, "email", email).
    Set e to checkRequired(e, "password", password).
    Set e to checkMinLength(e, "password", password, 8).
    Return e.

## Page /join

State:
    Let email be "".
    Let password be "".
    Let errors be a new Seq of FieldError.
    Let joined be false.

Actions:
    To submit:
        Set errors to validate(email, password).
        If isValid(errors):
            Set joined to true.

View:
    <main>
      <form id="join" on-submit.prevent={submit}>
        <input id="email" type="email" aria-label="Email" bind={email}>
        <p id="email-error">{errorFor(errors, "email")}</p>
        <input id="password" type="password" aria-label="Password" bind={password}>
        <p id="password-error">{errorFor(errors, "password")}</p>
        <button id="go" type="submit">Join</button>
      </form>
      {if joined:}<p id="welcome">Welcome.</p>{end}
    </main>

## Test: an empty form names each field's first problem

Submit "#join".
Expect that the text of "#email-error" is equal to "This is required.".
Expect that the text of "#password-error" is equal to "This is required.".
Expect that "#welcome" is hidden.

## Test: a field that passes says nothing

Type "ada@example.com" into "#email".
Type "short" into "#password".
Submit "#join".
Expect that the text of "#email-error" is equal to "".
Expect that the text of "#password-error" is equal to "Use at least 8 characters.".

## Test: a clean submission is accepted

Type "ada@example.com" into "#email".
Type "correct horse" into "#password".
Submit "#join".
Expect that the text of "#welcome" is equal to "Welcome.".
```

The same functions work anywhere, not only in a page. `errorSummary` joins every message, one per
line, for the summary a form puts above its fields:

```logos
## Main
Let mutable e be noErrors().
Set e to checkRequired(e, "name", "   ").
Set e to checkRange(e, "age", 130, 0, 120).
Set e to checkSame(e, "confirm", "tulip", "tulips", "The two passwords differ.").
Set e to checkRequired(e, "name", "").
Show errorSummary(e).
Show length of e.
Show errorFor(e, "age").
Show length of errorFor(e, "email").
Show isValid(noErrors()).
```

```output
This is required.
Choose a number from 0 to 120.
The two passwords differ.
3
Choose a number from 0 to 120.
0
true
```

`checkEmail` checks the shape of an address — one `@`, something before it, a dotted something
after it — and leaves an empty value to `checkRequired`, so an optional email field may stay blank.
Only a message arriving proves an address works.

<!-- generated from forms.lg by lgx_stdlib_guide_lock: ./scripts/release/lgx/gen-reference.sh -->

| Definition | What it is |
|---|---|
| `A FieldError has` | One complaint about a submission: the `field` it concerns and the `message` to show beside it. |
| `noErrors() -> Seq of FieldError` | An empty complaint list — the start of every validation. |
| `isValid(errors: Seq of FieldError) -> Bool` | Whether `errors` records no complaint at all. |
| `hasError(errors: Seq of FieldError, field: Text) -> Bool` | Whether `field` has a complaint recorded against it. |
| `errorFor(errors: Seq of FieldError, field: Text) -> Text` | The complaint against `field`, or `""` when there is none. |
| `addError(errors: Seq of FieldError, field: Text, message: Text) -> Seq of FieldError` | `errors` with `message` recorded against `field`. |
| `isBlank(t: Text) -> Bool` | Whether `t` is empty or nothing but whitespace. |
| `checkRequired(errors: Seq of FieldError, field: Text, value: Text) -> Seq of FieldError` | Complain when `value` is empty or all whitespace. |
| `checkMinLength(errors: Seq of FieldError, field: Text, value: Text, n: Int) -> Seq of FieldError` | Complain when `value` is shorter than `n` characters, counting after trimming. |
| `checkMaxLength(errors: Seq of FieldError, field: Text, value: Text, n: Int) -> Seq of FieldError` | Complain when `value` is longer than `n` characters, counting after trimming. |
| `checkRange(errors: Seq of FieldError, field: Text, value: Int, low: Int, high: Int) -> Seq of FieldError` | Complain when `value` is outside `low` to `high`, both included. |
| `checkSame(errors: Seq of FieldError, field: Text, a: Text, b: Text, message: Text) -> Seq of FieldError` | Complain when `a` and `b` differ — the password-confirmation check. |
| `looksLikeEmail(value: Text) -> Bool` | Whether `value`, trimmed, has the shape of an email address: one `@`, something before it, and a dot with text on both sides after it. |
| `checkEmail(errors: Seq of FieldError, field: Text, value: Text) -> Seq of FieldError` | Complain when `value` does not look like an email address. An empty value is left to `checkRequired`, so an optional field may be blank without complaint. |
| `errorSummary(errors: Seq of FieldError) -> Text` | Every complaint, one per line — the summary a form puts above its fields. |

<!-- end generated -->

## UI — `ui.lg`

[`examples/data_table`](../examples/data_table) pages a filtered, sorted table with this module.
Pagination is where the off-by-one errors live, and every function here answers in the language's
own terms: positions are 1-based, a page count is never 0, and the last page is short.

- `clampPage(page, total, perPage)` brings a requested page inside the table, so Next on the last
  page stays there.
- `pageStart(page, perPage)` to `pageEnd(page, perPage, total)` is the run of positions a page
  shows, ready for `item i of xs`. For an empty list the run is empty: the end is 0 and the start
  is 1.
- `pageCount(total, perPage)` is at least 1: an empty list still has a page, the one that says
  nothing is there.

The text helpers are filters: `{n | plural "person" "people"}` is `plural(n, "person", "people")`.

```logos-dom
## To everyone () -> Seq of Text:
    Let mutable out be a new Seq of Text.
    Push "Ada Lovelace" to out.
    Push "Grace Hopper" to out.
    Push "Katherine Johnson" to out.
    Push "Margaret Hamilton" to out.
    Push "Radia Perlman" to out.
    Return out.

## To pageOf (names: Seq of Text) and (page: Int) and (perPage: Int) -> Seq of Text:
    Let total be length of names.
    Let mutable out be a new Seq of Text.
    Let mutable i be pageStart(page, perPage).
    While i is at most pageEnd(page, perPage, total):
        Push item i of names to out.
        Set i to i + 1.
    Return out.

## Page /people

State:
    Let names be a new Seq of Text.
    Let shown be a new Seq of Text.
    Let page be 1.

Actions:
    When the page loads:
        Set names to everyone().
        Set shown to pageOf(names, page, 2).

    To next:
        Set page to clampPage(page + 1, length of names, 2).
        Set shown to pageOf(names, page, 2).

    To previous:
        Set page to clampPage(page - 1, length of names, 2).
        Set shown to pageOf(names, page, 2).

View:
    <main>
      <p id="count">{length of names | plural "person" "people"}</p>
      <ul>
        {for each n in shown, at index i:}
          <li id="row-{i}" class="person"><span class="initials">{n | initials}</span> <span class="name">{n | truncate 8}</span></li>
        {end}
      </ul>
      <p id="where">Page {page} of {pageCount(length of names, 2)}</p>
      <button id="previous" on-click={previous}>Previous</button>
      <button id="next" on-click={next}>Next</button>
    </main>

## Test: the first page shows the first two people

Expect that the text of "#count" is equal to "5 people".
Expect that the count of ".person" is equal to 2.
Expect that the text of "#row-1 .initials" is equal to "AL".
Expect that the text of "#row-2 .name" is equal to "Grace H…".
Expect that the text of "#where" is equal to "Page 1 of 3".

## Test: the last page is short and Next stays on it

Click "#next".
Click "#next".
Click "#next".
Expect that the text of "#where" is equal to "Page 3 of 3".
Expect that the count of ".person" is equal to 1.
Expect that the text of "#row-1 .initials" is equal to "RP".

## Test: Previous on the first page stays on it

Click "#previous".
Expect that the text of "#where" is equal to "Page 1 of 3".
Expect that the count of ".person" is equal to 2.
```

`truncate` marks a cut with `…` and counts the mark inside its limit, so the answer is never longer
than asked; `initials` treats any run of spaces as one separator.

<!-- generated from ui.lg by lgx_stdlib_guide_lock: ./scripts/release/lgx/gen-reference.sh -->

| Definition | What it is |
|---|---|
| `pageCount(total: Int, perPage: Int) -> Int` | How many pages `total` items make at `perPage` each. |
| `clampPage(page: Int, total: Int, perPage: Int) -> Int` | `page` brought inside `1` to `pageCount(total, perPage)`. |
| `pageStart(page: Int, perPage: Int) -> Int` | The 1-based index of the first item on `page`. |
| `pageEnd(page: Int, perPage: Int, total: Int) -> Int` | The 1-based index of the last item on `page`, never past `total`. |
| `truncate(t: Text, n: Int) -> Text` | `t` cut to at most `n` characters, marked with `…` when anything was removed. |
| `plural(n: Int, one: Text, many: Text) -> Text` | `n` with the word that agrees with it: `1 item`, `2 items`, `0 items`. |
| `initials(name: Text) -> Text` | The first letter of each word of `name`, run together: `Ada Lovelace` is `AL`. |

<!-- end generated -->

## Sessions — `session.lg`

[`examples/login`](../examples/login) is a signed-in site that never calls this module by name.
A `## Session` block declares what a session holds, and the compiler writes the rest: the
cookie is the session's fields, hex-encoded, followed by a signature (`signSession`); every
request's cookie is checked (`verifySession`) and a forged or edited one reads as a new, empty
session; `csrf()` is this session's token (`csrfToken`) for a form to carry; and a request that
changes state without the right token is refused with 403 before its route runs (`csrfValid`).

```logos
## Session
    a user, which is Text.

## Route POST /login (name: Text) -> Response:
    Set the session's user to name.
    Return redirectTo("/me").

## Route GET /me -> View:
    <main>
      {if the session's user is equal to "":}
        <p id="who">Nobody is signed in.</p>
      {else:}
        <p id="who">Signed in as {the session's user}.</p>
      {end}
    </main>

## Main

Serve on port 8080.

## Test: a visitor with no session is nobody

Expect that route("GET", "/me") contains "Nobody is signed in.".

## Test: a form post without its CSRF token is refused before the route runs

Expect that routeStatus("POST", "/login") is equal to 403.
```

The key the cookies are signed with is `sessionSecret()`: `LOGOS_SESSION_SECRET` when it is set,
otherwise a random secret made once per process — sessions then end when the server restarts, and
nobody can forge one.

The functions are ordinary LOGOS, and they are what the sentences above become. A signature is
checked against the value it signs, so a cookie carrying someone else's name with a real signature
is refused, and a CSRF token is bound to one session:

```logos
## Main
Let secret be "a secret for this example".
Let cookie be signSession(secret, "ada").
Inspect verifySession(secret, cookie):
    When Some (who):
        Show "signed in: " + who.
    When None:
        Show "refused".
Inspect verifySession(secret, "mallory|" + sessionMac(cookie)):
    When Some (who):
        Show "signed in: " + who.
    When None:
        Show "refused".
Show csrfValid(secret, cookie, csrfToken(secret, cookie)).
Show csrfValid(secret, cookie, csrfToken(secret, "another session")).
```

```output
signed in: ada
refused
true
false
```

<!-- generated from session.lg by lgx_stdlib_guide_lock: ./scripts/release/lgx/gen-reference.sh -->

| Definition | What it is |
|---|---|
| `textUpTo(t: Text, n: Int) -> Text` | `t` up to and including its `n`th character; `""` when `n` is not positive. |
| `textFrom(t: Text, n: Int) -> Text` | `t` after its `n`th character; the whole of `t` when `n` is 0. |
| `lastSeparator(t: Text) -> Int` | The 1-based position of the LAST `\|` in `t`, or 0 when there is none. |
| `macHex(secret: Text, msg: Text) -> Text` | `msg` authenticated under `secret`, as lowercase hex. |
| `sameTextInConstantTime(a: Text, b: Text) -> Bool` | Whether `a` and `b` are the same text, reading every byte of two texts of one length before it answers. |
| `signSession(secret: Text, value: Text) -> Text` | `value`, followed by its signature — the cookie a server hands out. |
| `sessionMac(cookie: Text) -> Text` | The signature half of a cookie, for a caller that wants to inspect it. |
| `verifySession(secret: Text, cookie: Text) -> Option of Text` | The value a cookie carries, or `none` when its signature does not check. |
| `csrfToken(secret: Text, session: Text) -> Text` | A CSRF token BOUND to one session. |
| `csrfValid(secret: Text, session: Text, token: Text) -> Bool` | Whether `token` is the CSRF token for this `session`. |
| `hexText(t: Text) -> Text` | The UTF-8 bytes of `t` as lowercase hexadecimal; `unhexText` is the way back. |
| `unhexText(h: Text) -> Text` | The text a `hexText` came from. Invalid hex answers `""` rather than trapping, because a cookie is attacker-controlled input. |
| `sessionField(payload: Text, i: Int) -> Text` | Field `i` of a session payload — counting from 1, as LOGOS indices do — or `""` when the payload does not carry one. |
| `sessionInt(payload: Text, i: Int) -> Int` | Field `i` of a session payload as a whole number, or `0` when it is absent or not one. |
| `sessionBool(payload: Text, i: Int) -> Bool` | Field `i` of a session payload as a truth value. Anything that is not `true` is false, which is the safe direction for a flag a visitor holds a cookie for. |
| `sessionSecret() -> Text` | The secret every session cookie is signed with. |
| `randomSecret() -> Text` | A fresh unguessable secret — 8 random 31-bit numbers in hex. |

<!-- end generated -->

## Where this is tested

Every page here is mounted and rendered on the tree-walker and the VM, compiled for the browser,
and has its tests run by `canonical_teaching_lock`; every program compiles, prints what its
`output` block shows and passes its tests under `doc_examples`. The definition tables are held
equal to the modules' own notes, and each section's example project is held to exist and to use
its module, by `lgx_stdlib_guide_lock`. The modules themselves are pinned by `forms_lock`,
`ui_lock`, `session_lock`, `session_block_lock` and `csrf_lock`.

# LOGOS Error Catalog

Every diagnostic the LOGOS toolchain emits, keyed by its stable
`logos-diagnostic/1` code — the `code` field of `largo check --json`,
`largo run --json`, and the MCP `logos_check` tool. Look a code up here
or with `largo explain <code>`.

Generated from `logicaffeine_language::diagnostic::catalog()`. Do not
edit by hand; run `./scripts/release/gen-error-catalog.sh` after changing
`ParseErrorKind`.

## `unexpected-token`

- **Severity**: error
- **Variant**: `UnexpectedToken`

**Example**:

```text
expected a period ('.'), found a comma (',')
```

> I was following your sentence but stumbled here: I expected a period ('.'), and found a comma (',') instead. The structure so far commits me to a period ('.') next. Is a word missing just before this, or did two thoughts run together? Splitting the sentence in two often shows which.

## `expected-content-word`

- **Severity**: error
- **Variant**: `ExpectedContentWord`

**Example**:

```text
expected a content word, found a comma (',')
```

> This spot needs a content word — a noun, a verb, or an adjective — but I found a comma (',') instead. Content words carry the meaning; the little words only arrange them. What thing, action, or quality did you mean to name here? Put that word in and the sentence grounds itself.

## `expected-copula`

- **Severity**: error
- **Variant**: `ExpectedCopula`

**Example**:

```text
expected 'is' or 'are'
```

> The subject here is waiting for 'is' or 'are' to link it to its predicate. English predication runs through a copula — without one, the two halves never connect. What is the subject supposed to BE? Write it as 'X is Y' ('are' for plurals).

## `unknown-quantifier`

- **Severity**: error
- **Variant**: `UnknownQuantifier`

**Example**:

```text
expected a quantifier, found a comma (',')
```

> I needed a quantifier here — a word like 'all', 'some', or 'no' — but found a comma (','). Quantifiers say how many things the sentence talks about, and that choice decides the whole logical shape. How many did you mean: every one, at least one, or none? Lead with the word that says so.

## `unknown-modal`

- **Severity**: error
- **Variant**: `UnknownModal`

**Example**:

```text
expected a modal, found a comma (',')
```

> I needed a modal here — 'must', 'can', 'may', 'should' — but found a comma (','). Modals set the strength of the claim: necessity, possibility, permission, obligation. Which strength did you mean? Pick the modal that carries it and the logic follows.

## `expected-verb`

- **Severity**: error
- **Variant**: `ExpectedVerb`

**Example**:

```text
expected a verb, found a comma (',')
```

> Every sentence needs a verb, and this one's verb should appear here — I found a comma (',') instead. The verb names the action or state everything else hangs on. What is the subject doing (or being)? Give the sentence that verb.

## `expected-temporal-adverb`

- **Severity**: error
- **Variant**: `ExpectedTemporalAdverb`

**Example**:

```text
expected a temporal adverb
```

> I expected a time word here — 'yesterday', 'tomorrow', 'always'. Temporal adverbs anchor the sentence on the timeline, and this construction promised one. When does this happen? Say it with a temporal adverb, or drop the construction that required one.

## `expected-presupposition-trigger`

- **Severity**: error
- **Variant**: `ExpectedPresuppositionTrigger`

**Example**:

```text
expected a presupposition trigger
```

> I expected a presupposition trigger here — a word like 'stopped', 'realized', or 'regrets'. These verbs quietly assume something was already true; that hidden assumption is what this construction works with. What background fact is being taken for granted? The trigger word is what carries it.

## `expected-focus-particle`

- **Severity**: error
- **Variant**: `ExpectedFocusParticle`

**Example**:

```text
expected a focus particle
```

> I expected a focus particle here — 'only', 'even', 'just'. Focus particles single out one part of the sentence against its alternatives. Which word should the emphasis land on? Put the particle directly before it.

## `expected-scopal-adverb`

- **Severity**: error
- **Variant**: `ExpectedScopalAdverb`

**Example**:

```text
expected a scopal adverb
```

> I expected a scopal adverb here — a word like 'necessarily' or 'possibly' that comments on the whole claim rather than the verb alone. Is the adverb meant to cover the entire sentence? If it only describes the action, it belongs next to the verb instead.

## `expected-superlative-adjective`

- **Severity**: error
- **Variant**: `ExpectedSuperlativeAdjective`

**Example**:

```text
expected a superlative adjective
```

> I expected a superlative here — 'tallest', 'fastest', the '-est' form. A superlative ranks one thing against all the others, and that is the comparison this sentence set up. Are you comparing against everything, or just one other thing? Use '-est' for everything, '-er than' for one.

## `expected-comparative-adjective`

- **Severity**: error
- **Variant**: `ExpectedComparativeAdjective`

**Example**:

```text
expected a comparative adjective
```

> I expected a comparative here — 'taller', 'faster', the '-er' form. A comparative weighs exactly two things against each other. What quality are the two compared on? Name it in its '-er' form and follow with 'than'.

## `expected-than`

- **Severity**: error
- **Variant**: `ExpectedThan`

**Example**:

```text
expected 'than' to complete the comparison
```

> A comparative opened a comparison, and 'than' introduces the other side — but it is missing here. Taller than what, exactly? Add 'than' plus the thing being compared against.

## `expected-number`

- **Severity**: error
- **Variant**: `ExpectedNumber`

**Example**:

```text
expected a number
```

> This measure phrase needs a number — '2', '3.14' — and none appeared. A measure without a quantity measures nothing. How much, exactly? Put the number in front of the unit.

## `empty-restriction`

- **Severity**: error
- **Variant**: `EmptyRestriction`

**Example**:

```text
empty relative clause
```

> This relative clause is empty — 'the X that ...' with nothing after 'that'. A restriction narrows the noun down, so an empty one narrows nothing. Which ones did you mean? State the property that picks them out, or drop the 'that' entirely.

## `gapping-resolution-failed`

- **Severity**: error
- **Variant**: `GappingResolutionFailed`

**Example**:

```text
no verb to borrow for the gapped clause
```

> This reads like a gapped construction — '... and Mary, a pear' — where the verb is borrowed from the previous clause, but I found no verb there to borrow. What is the second subject doing? Either repeat the verb outright, or make sure the first clause states it plainly.

## `stative-progressive-conflict`

- **Severity**: error
- **Variant**: `StativeProgressiveConflict`

**Example**:

```text
stative verb used in the progressive
```

> A stative verb like 'know' or 'love' is in the progressive here, and states do not run in progress — they simply hold or they don't. Is this a state or an ongoing activity? States take the simple form ('knows'); only activities take '-ing'.

## `undefined-variable`

- **Severity**: error
- **Variant**: `UndefinedVariable`
- **Quickfix**: Did you mean '<nearest definition>'?
- **Guide**: <https://github.com/Brahmastra-Labs/logicaffeine/blob/main/LOGOS_QUICKGUIDE.md#2-variables--mutation>

**Example**:

```text
'x' is not declared
```

> I found 'x', but nothing has declared it. Every variable starts life in a Let — reading a name before it exists gives me no value to read. Where should 'x' get its first value? Add 'Let x be ...' above this line, or check the spelling against the name you declared.

## `use-after-move`

- **Severity**: error
- **Variant**: `UseAfterMove`
- **Quickfix**: Use 'a copy of …' instead
- **Guide**: <https://github.com/Brahmastra-Labs/logicaffeine/blob/main/LOGOS_QUICKGUIDE.md#13-output>

**Example**:

```text
cannot use 'x' after giving it away
```

> Cannot use 'x' after giving it away. 'Give x to ...' transferred ownership — 'x' belongs to the receiver now, and this later use has nothing left to hold. Who really needs to own 'x' here? To lend it and keep it, 'Show x'; to hand over a duplicate, give 'a copy of x'.

## `is-value-equality`

- **Severity**: warning
- **Variant**: `IsValueEquality`
- **Quickfix**: Use 'equals' for value comparison
- **Guide**: <https://github.com/Brahmastra-Labs/logicaffeine/blob/main/LOGOS_QUICKGUIDE.md#3-arithmetic-comparison-logic-bitwise>

**Example**:

```text
'x is 5' compares values; use 'equals'
```

> 'x is 5' reads as a type or predicate claim — 'is' asks what something IS, not which value it holds. Value comparison is spelled 'equals'. Are you asking what 'x' is, or whether it holds 5? For the value question, write 'x equals 5'.

## `zero-index`

- **Severity**: info
- **Variant**: `ZeroIndex`
- **Quickfix**: Use 1-based indexing
- **Guide**: <https://github.com/Brahmastra-Labs/logicaffeine/blob/main/LOGOS_QUICKGUIDE.md#5-collections>

**Example**:

```text
indices start at 1; there is no item 0
```

> This asks for item 0, but LOGOS indices start at 1 — in English, 'the 1st item' is the first one; there is no item 0. Which element did you want? The first is 'item 1 of xs' — the zero-based habit is the only thing to unlearn.

## `expected-statement`

- **Severity**: error
- **Variant**: `ExpectedStatement`

**Example**:

```text
expected a statement
```

> I expected a statement here — a sentence that does something, like 'Let', 'Set', 'Show', or 'Return'. What should happen at this point in the program? Start the line with the verb that does it, and end with a period.

## `expected-keyword`

- **Severity**: error
- **Variant**: `ExpectedKeyword`

**Example**:

```text
expected the word 'to'
```

> This construction needs the word 'to' here to complete its shape. Statement forms have fixed connecting words — they are the joints of the sentence. Which form did you start? Insert 'to' where I stopped, or compare your line against that form's example.

## `expected-expression`

- **Severity**: error
- **Variant**: `ExpectedExpression`

**Example**:

```text
expected an expression
```

> I expected an expression here — a value: a number, a variable, a call, or a computation. Something just before this (a 'be', a 'to', an operator) promised a value that never arrived. What value should flow into this spot? Write it, or remove the connector that promised it.

## `expected-identifier`

- **Severity**: error
- **Variant**: `ExpectedIdentifier`

**Example**:

```text
expected a name
```

> I expected a name here — an identifier for a variable, function, or field. This position says which thing the statement acts on, so a keyword or symbol cannot stand in. What is the thing called? Use its declared name, or declare it first with Let.

## `respectively-length-mismatch`

- **Severity**: error
- **Variant**: `RespectivelyLengthMismatch`

**Example**:

```text
'respectively' lists differ: 2 subject(s) vs 3 object(s)
```

> 'Respectively' pairs the two lists one-to-one, but the subject side has 2 element(s) and the object side has 3. With uneven lists, something ends up with no partner. Which pairing did you intend? Even the lists out, or split the sentence so each pairing is explicit.

## `type-mismatch`

- **Severity**: error
- **Variant**: `TypeMismatch`, `TypeMismatchDetailed`
- **Guide**: <https://github.com/Brahmastra-Labs/logicaffeine/blob/main/LOGOS_QUICKGUIDE.md#2-variables--mutation>

**Example**:

```text
expected 'Int', found 'Text'
```

> This slot is typed 'Int', but the value here is 'Text'. LOGOS holds every value to its declared type — that agreement is what the later guarantees stand on. Which side is right, the annotation or the value? Change the one that is lying.

**Example**:

```text
expected 'Int', found 'Text' (in argument 2 of 'compute')
```

> I expected 'Int' here but found 'Text' (in argument 2 of 'compute'). The two sides of this position must agree on one type. Which side has it right? Adjust the annotation or the value so they tell the same story.

## `infinite-type`

- **Severity**: error
- **Variant**: `InfiniteType`

**Example**:

```text
infinite type: T would contain itself
```

> This would make an infinite type: T would have to equal Seq of T, which contains it — a type inside itself, forever. This usually means a value is being folded into its own container. Did you mean to push into the collection rather than rebuild it? A named struct or one level of indirection breaks the cycle.

## `arity-mismatch`

- **Severity**: error
- **Variant**: `ArityMismatch`
- **Guide**: <https://github.com/Brahmastra-Labs/logicaffeine/blob/main/LOGOS_QUICKGUIDE.md#7-functions--closures>

**Example**:

```text
'greet' takes 2 argument(s), but this call passes 1
```

> 'greet' takes 2 argument(s), but this call passes 1. A call must fill every parameter — each one is a promise the function body relies on. Which parameter went missing, or which extra snuck in? Line the call up against the function's '## To' header.

## `field-not-found`

- **Severity**: error
- **Variant**: `FieldNotFound`
- **Guide**: <https://github.com/Brahmastra-Labs/logicaffeine/blob/main/LOGOS_QUICKGUIDE.md#8-structs-enums--field-access>

**Example**:

```text
'Point' has no field named 'z'
```

> 'Point' has no field named 'z'. A struct's fields are fixed at its definition — reads cannot invent new ones. Available fields: x, y. Did you mean one of those, or should the '## A Point has:' definition grow a 'z'?

## `not-a-function`

- **Severity**: error
- **Variant**: `NotAFunction`
- **Guide**: <https://github.com/Brahmastra-Labs/logicaffeine/blob/main/LOGOS_QUICKGUIDE.md#7-functions--closures>

**Example**:

```text
cannot call a value of type 'Int'
```

> This tries to call a value of type 'Int', but only functions and closures can be called. Parentheses after a name mean 'invoke this'. Did you want a function with a similar name, or is this variable shadowing the function you meant?

## `invalid-refinement-predicate`

- **Severity**: error
- **Variant**: `InvalidRefinementPredicate`

**Example**:

```text
refinement predicate is not checkable
```

> This refinement predicate is not one I can check — refinements are comparisons over the declared name, like 'x > 0' or 'n < 100'. What must always be true of this value? State it as a simple comparison; anything richer belongs in an Assert.

## `grammar-error`

- **Severity**: warning
- **Variant**: `GrammarError`

**Example**:

```text
grammar: its vs it's
```

> Grammar: its vs it's. Small grammar slips change the logical reading, so I stop rather than guess. Which meaning did you intend? Adjust the wording — the right form usually reads aloud correctly.

## `scope-violation`

- **Severity**: error
- **Variant**: `ScopeViolation`

**Example**:

```text
scope: pronoun trapped in negation
```

> Scope problem: pronoun trapped in negation. A pronoun can only reach referents its clause can see — things introduced under a negation or inside an 'or' are walled off from later sentences. Who is the pronoun meant to point at? Name the referent outright, or introduce it outside the wall.

## `unresolved-pronoun`

- **Severity**: error
- **Variant**: `UnresolvedPronoun`

**Example**:

```text
pronoun 'she' has no antecedent
```

> This pronoun ('she') has nothing to refer to — no earlier sentence introduced a matching referent this clause can reach. Pronouns only look backward through accessible discourse. Who is 'she' here? Introduce that referent in an earlier sentence, or use the name directly.

## `trailing-tokens`

- **Severity**: error
- **Variant**: `TrailingTokens`

**Example**:

```text
input left over, beginning with a comma (',')
```

> I understood the sentence up to here, but the rest — beginning with a comma (',') — does not fit the structure I built. Accepting it would silently drop that meaning, and LOGOS never drops meaning. Is a connective missing, or are two sentences sharing one period? End the first thought with '.' and start fresh.

## `ast-too-deep`

- **Severity**: error
- **Variant**: `AstTooDeep`

**Example**:

```text
AST nests 3000 levels deep; the limit is 2048
```

> This program nests expressions or blocks 3000 levels deep, past the current 2048-level limit — a tower this tall usually comes from generated code, and every downstream walker would overflow on it. Could each layer land in its own 'Let'? Intermediate bindings reset the depth to one; or raise the gate with LOGOS_MAX_AST_DEPTH=4096 if your stacks are deep.

## `custom`

- **Severity**: error
- **Variant**: `Custom`

**Example**:

```text
zone escape
```

> zone escape
